description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of mathematical problem categories across different educational levels—High School, Olympiad-level, and University-level—as used in the MathOdyssey benchmark for evaluating large language models. The chart is divided into ten distinct slices, each labeled with the topic, educational level, percentage of total problems, and absolute count in parentheses. The largest segment is “Algebra – University-level” at 21.19% (82 problems), followed by “Algebra – High School” at 17.83% (69 problems), and “Pre-Calculus – High School” at 14.21% (55 problems). Other notable segments include “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” (9.56%, 37 problems), “Geometry – Olympiad-level” (6.46%, 25 problems), and “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” (6.46%, 25 problems). Smaller slices include “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” (6.20%, 24 problems), “Probability – University-level” (5.43%, 21 problems), “Statistics – University-level” (4.39%, 17 problems), and “Differential Equations – University-level” and “Geometry – High School” both at 3.62% (14 problems each). “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” is the smallest segment at 1.03% (4 problems). The chart uses distinct colors for each slice and includes percentage and count labels outside the pie, connected by lines, with no legend required as all categories are directly labeled. The segments are arranged roughly in descending order of size, starting from the top-left and moving clockwise.
